It's not just gas prices going up...

Grocery prices and electricity also jumping.
These are the basic costs for most Americans.


Kevin Gordon (@KevRGordon)

CPI food at home (essentially grocery prices) jumped by 0.68% m/m in April ... largest increase since August 2022





— https://nitter.net/KevRGordon/status/2054180728603038034#m

Americans are trying to work more hours to keep up as gas and food prices rise. 

Even so, real average weekly earnings **Decreased** in April as inflation ate up all the wage gains and extra hours worked.

Real weekly earnings for all workers: -0.2% in April
Real weekly earnings for "rank and file" workers: -0.3% in April

JUST IN: Inflation is now eating up all wage gains for the first time in about three years. This is painful for Americans and a true financial squeeze.

CPI Inflation in past year: 3.8%
Wage gains: in past year: 3.6%

JUST IN: U.S. inflation jumped to 3.8% (y/y) in April--> the highest in three years. This is painful for Americans, especially moderate-income households.

Inflation rose 0.6% in the month of April due to soaring gas prices that accounted for over 40% of the increase. Rising shelter and food prices also pushed up inflation.

Core inflation (which excludes food and energy came in at 2.8% (y/y) in April

Kudos to @JustinWolfers on the launch of Platypus Economics, a new media initiative to explain economics to everyone.

We need more of this!
(And I hope @BetseyStevenson will be a regular on the show, too)

Inflation is wiping out wage gains.
This is the big Achilles Heel in the US economy.

April wage growth: 3.6% 
April inflation expected to be ~4%

Wages are being eaten up by inflation due to the war in Iran. This is a big shift from the past several years when wages were growing well above inflation. 

Yes, workers have jobs, but this is a squeeze.

Is the hiring recession over in the United States?
We are seeing encouraging signs...

Average monthly job gains so far in 2026 = 76,000, well above the anemic 10k monthly avg. for 2025.

Unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3%

More industries hiring than just healthcare.


Heather Long (@byHeatherLong)

JUST IN: Good news. The US economy added a strong 115,000 jobs in April (and March was revised higher to 185,000!) The unemployment rate stayed at 4.3%. Hiring was strong in healthcare (about

JUST IN: Good news. The US economy added a strong 115,000 jobs in April (and March was revised higher to 185,000!) The unemployment rate stayed at 4.3%. Hiring was strong in healthcare (about 1/3 of job gains in April), retail and transportation/warehouse.

The bad news = Inflation is about to eat up wage gains.

Wage growth: 3.6% in past year --> That’s likely to be eaten up by April inflation of ~4%

#jobs

There was a big bounce back in the official U.S. hiring rate in March.

3.5% hiring rate is the highest in almost 2 years!

Strong hiring in March in transportation, warehousing, utilities (+108,000). And solid hiring in professional/biz services (+165,000) and hospitality (+124,000).

The war in Iran is likely to halt progress. But any sign of a hiring pickup is welcome news after the "hiring recession" in the past year or so.

Business investment contributed **more** to GDP in Q1 than consumer spending.

This is an AI economy now.

Personal consumption contribution to Q1 GDP: 1.08

(Joey's great chart shows the biz investment in green vs. consumption in yellow)

US Real GDP came in at a 2% annualized growth rate in Q1 2026 data released this morning. Consumption & investment increased, government output rose, and the tra

Important: The US savings rate fell to 3.6% in March. That's the lowest since fall 2022 (the "revenge spend" era). And it's frankly one of the lower readings of all time.

American households are getting squeezed.
Many are not able to save right now as they face ongoing high costs for gas, electricity, and healthcare.

Bottom line: There's less cushion if a downturn or economic slowdown occurs.

This is the AI economy now.
Just incredible to see the +10.4% jump in business investment in Q1. That's the highest since Q2 2023 (when the big semiconductor factory buildout was underway. Now it's all AI)

Notice consumption: +1.6%. That's pretty tepid. One of the weaker consumer spending readings lately.
